seoTitle: Create a Table in Squarespace Without a Plugin
metaDescription: Add a pricing, spec, or comparison table in Squarespace using a Code Block with HTML and CSS, since there's no built-in table tool.
intro: Squarespace doesn't have a built-in feature for inserting tables through its visual editor, but you can still build one using a Code Block with basic HTML and CSS. This guide walks through adding the table markup and styling it to match your site.

steps.heading: Open the page and enter edit mode
steps.body: Log in to Squarespace, navigate to the page where you want the table, and click Edit to enter the page's edit mode.

steps.heading: Add a Code Block
steps.body: Click Add Block, then choose Code from the available options — this lets you insert custom HTML directly onto the page.

steps.heading: Enter your table's HTML
steps.body: Type or paste your table code, starting with a table tag, row tags for each row, and cell tags for each cell, then click Save to place it on the page.

steps.heading: Style the table with CSS
steps.body: Go to the Custom CSS section under the Design menu and add styles controlling text size, borders, and colors for your table.

steps.heading: Scope your CSS to avoid site-wide changes
steps.body: Give your table a unique ID or class in the HTML, then reference that identifier in your CSS so the styling only affects this table.

faq.question: Does Squarespace have a built-in table tool?
faq.answer: No, there's no native table block in the visual editor, so a Code Block with HTML and CSS is the standard workaround.

faq.question: Do I need coding experience to add a table this way?
faq.answer: Basic HTML and CSS knowledge helps, but plenty of templates and online resources exist to help you craft the table code you need.

faq.question: How do I stop my table's CSS from affecting other tables on my site?
faq.answer: Give the table a unique ID or class and reference that specific identifier in your CSS instead of styling the table element globally.

faq.question: Can I use this method for pricing tables and comparison tables too?
faq.answer: Yes, the same Code Block approach works for pricing tables, comparison tables, or any structured tabular content.
